title: Opaque chunk handoff and async kernel cohesion to reduce TP comm/compute stalls
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Tensor-parallel inference on >4 GPUs occasionally hits short, repeated stalls when small microbatches interleave heavy NCCL collectives and short compute kernels. Root cause analysis showed repeated host-device synchronization and fragmented collective chunk ownership causing NCCL stream contention and KV-cache eviction thrash. This PR implements an end-to-end change to reduce those stalls by introducing an opaque chunk allocator (comm-owned chunk descriptors), a comm->compute handoff path, and an async kernel cohesion layer that coalesces short compute kernels to reduce launch overhead.

Summary of changes (single continuous section): added a comm-side opaque chunk allocator that hands ownership of contiguous tensor chunks to the NCCL comm thread without exposing physical offsets to the compute stage; added a lightweight comm->compute handover RPC inside the runtime that schedules dependent compute launches onto the same CUDA stream (or a tightly-coupled stream pair) to avoid cross-stream synchronization; implemented an async kernel cohesion module that buffers tiny kernels produced by model dispatch into a microbatch-local launch batch to amortize kernel launch costs and reduce inter-kernel device-side dependency checks; introduced an adaptive NCCL concurrency limiter that observes in-flight channel contention and throttles the number of concurrent collectives per node to smooth host CPU scheduling spikes; added a KV cache handshake that pins frequently accessed KV slabs to device-resident reserved pages during high-churn workloads to avoid eviction-induced allgathers.

Checklist: - [x] Feature design doc attached to Linear ENG-4127 - [x] Microbench harness updated to include p50/p95/p99 per-token latency and throughput traces - [x] Unit + integration tests for comm allocator and handoff - [x] Manual perf runs on 8xA100 and 4xH100 clusters - [x] CI passes (lint, unit, integration)

Benchmark highlights (8 GPU TP8, seq_len=2048, batch 8 continuous batching workload): - Baseline (main at time of branch): p99 token latency 62.3 ms, throughput 1120 tokens/s - This PR: p99 token latency 50.9 ms (-18.2%), throughput 1254 tokens/s (+12%), CPU offload jitter reduced by ~35% (measured by scheduler run-queue sampling).

Design notes and motivation: The core idea is to reduce host-mediated coordination and reduce inter-stream fences by giving the comm runtime authoritative ownership over contiguous pieces of communication payload and enabling a single-shot handoff to compute that preserves stream locality. The opaque chunk descriptor is intentionally minimal (ID + length + device affinity) so compute never needs to reason about physical offsets; this allows the comm layer to coalesce chunk placements and avoid producing fragmented host pinned ranges that previously caused NCCL to thrash. The async kernel cohesion is conservative (configurable threshold) — for very long kernels it defers to the prior behavior to avoid increased tail latency for heavy compute.

Commits summary: single logical feature branch squashed from 7 commits (design, allocator impl, handoff RPC, cohesion buffer, KV handshake, tests, microbench updates). Commit messages are summarized in Linear.

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/tp/comm_allocator.cc (.h) - runtime/tp/comm_handoff_rpc.cc (.h) - runtime/tp/async_kernel_cohesion.cc (.h) - runtime/tp/nccl_throttle.cc - runtime/tp/kvhandshake.cc - runtime/tests/tp_comm_harness.cc - perf/microbench/tp_continuous_batching.yaml - docs/design/tp-opaque-chunk.md - build/bazel/BUILD.runtime - examples/tp/bench_presets.yaml

Testing and CI: The change required expanding the TP unit tests to include simulated interleaved tiny kernels and collectives. Integration tests were run on internal staging clusters (4xA100, 8xA100, 4xH100) with a smoke harness that validates correctness of outputs (bitwise identical for deterministic runs) and measures tail latencies. CI initially failed on flaky host-side race (fixed by adding a light-weight atomic handover fence and timeout), then passed on rerun.

Review conversation (summary, single string): Reviewer Liam: "Nice direction, reduced p99 on my 8xA100 run too. Please justify the opaque descriptor shape and add doc about future compatibility with NVSHMEM-managed slabs."; Author (Maya): "Added design doc and compatibility notes in docs/design/tp-opaque-chunk.md; kept descriptor minimal to preserve forward compatibility."; Reviewer Rosa: "Concern about degrading long-kernel latency when cohesion batches multiple heavy kernels."; Author: "Cohesion has a runtime-configurable threshold; default set to 2 ms kernel cost — updated tests to assert no regression beyond 1% for kernels >8ms."; Reviewer Ethan: "KV handshake looks promising but needs metrics exposed in console."; Author: "Added two new metrics: tp.kvslab.pinned_count and tp.comm.handoff_latency and added dashboard YAML in perf/microbench."; Approval: all reviewers approved after two iterations; PR merged via squash on 2026-02-18.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Changes are guarded by a runtime flag --tp-opaque-chunk-handoff (default on for new clusters) and a knob --async-kernel-cohesion-threshold-ms. The KV pinning is conservative and will not pin pages below a per-process memory threshold to avoid OOM risk.

Release notes: - Improved TP multi-GPU inference latency and throughput via opaque comm chunk handoff and async kernel cohesion (p99 -18% measured on internal workloads). - Added KV slab pinning handshake to reduce eviction-induced collectives. - New runtime flags to control handoff and cohesion behavior.

Related work: follows-up from ENG-3192 (continuous batching improvements) and complements ENG-2310 (kv-cache eviction fixes).

Known limitations and follow-ups: - NVSHMEM integration is not implemented in this PR; design doc includes the extension plan. - We observed modest CPU-side overhead (1-2%) for the comm allocator bookkeeping; follow-up optimizations planned (ENG-4198).
